results.note: Asserts request URL starts with the asset-metrics endpoint, params assets=btc/metrics=CapMVRVCur, and neither api_key/apikey query params nor authorization/x-cm-api-key headers are present. Not marked integration, so it ran under the reported 'test' gate (exit 0).

coinmetrics.py's _fetch_btc_metric checks _coinmetrics_error_type for 'bad_parameter' before any model validation and returns Error(FETCH_FAILED, detail=message); test confirms message is in detail and .value raises AttributeError. Covered by the passing 'test' gate.

Mocked 403/'forbidden' response maps to Unavailable(PAYWALLED), distinct from Error(FETCH_FAILED); ran under the passing 'test' gate. The story also demands proof against the real CapRealUSD endpoint specifically: tests/test_coinmetrics_fetcher.py:232 test_live_coinmetrics_caprealusd_is_paywalled_on_community_tier calls _fetch_btc_metric('CapRealUSD') with no mock, but it is @pytest.mark.integration and none of the reported deterministic gates ran with the integration marker included (default addopts is '-m not integration', and the only other reported gate is a bare mypy run) — so the 'real endpoint confirmed forbidden' half of this criterion has no exit-code proof, only a structurally correct but unexecuted-per-the-given-gates test.

Both CoinMetricsAssetMetricsEntry (line 147) and CoinMetricsAssetMetricsResponse (line 157) carry extra='forbid', frozen=True. Test asserts ValidationError on an added field ('extra_forbidden'), a renamed CapMVRVCur field, and a retyped (non-string) value ('string_type'). Ran under the passing 'test' gate.

Two consecutive fetch_btc_mvrv calls sharing one CoinMetricsRateLimiter (fake clock/sleeper) are asserted to be spaced 0.7s apart and both succeed against a mock server that 429s anything closer than 0.625s. This is a real multi-call proof, not a single lucky request. Caveat: the rate limiter is opt-in — fetch_btc_mvrv(rate_limiter=None) (its default) performs zero throttling, since _fetch_btc_metric only calls rate_limiter.wait() 'if rate_limiter is not None'; there is no module-level shared limiter, so any future caller that forgets to construct and thread one through gets no rate limiting at all. The criterion's literal test requirement is met; the wiring discipline for later stories is fragile.
Matches okx.py's pattern (Error(FETCH_FAILED) with status code in detail, .value raising AttributeError). Ran under the passing 'test' gate.

Asserts source_timestamp equals the response's own 'time' field and is strictly < now for a past value, and that a present-timestamp row yields Error(FETCH_FAILED) with 'future' in detail and no .value — the same F11 rule as okx.py. Ran under the passing 'test' gate.

Calls fetch_btc_mvrv() with no injected client/mock, so it goes through the real httpx.get path to the production Coin Metrics endpoint (the public entry point, not an isolated internal call) and asserts a positive value with a past source_timestamp. Structurally this is genuine, unmocked integration coverage. However it is @pytest.mark.integration and none of the three reported deterministic gates (typecheck, plain 'pytest -q', mypy --strict) actually execute integration-marked tests — pyproject's default addopts is '-m not integration' and no gate here overrides that (unlike the precedent pattern where a story's own C9 gate cleared addopts to run everything). So there is no exit-code proof this specific test was run and passed for this diff; the evidence is limited to the test's correct structure.
Reported gate 'US-701-C9: exit 0 [uv run mypy ingest --strict]' is exactly the command the criterion names, and it exited 0.

note: All test-method criteria (C1-C2, C4-C7) are backed by named, non-integration tests that ran under the reported green 'test' gate, and C9 by its own literal mypy gate. C3 and C8 both have well-formed, genuinely unmocked integration tests hitting the real Coin Metrics endpoint through the public fetch_btc_mvrv/_fetch_btc_metric functions, but no reported gate actually executed pytest with the integration marker included, so their 'proven against the real endpoint' claims rest on code inspection rather than an executed pass. One real design smell: the rate limiter is opt-in per-call (fetch_btc_mvrv defaults to rate_limiter=None, which skips throttling entirely), so the pattern this story is meant to establish for four more registry entries only works if every future caller remembers to construct and share a CoinMetricsRateLimiter — nothing enforces that by default.
